tool.name: mirtop gff
tool.description: annotate miRNA and isomiR reads as mirGFF3
tool.command: #import re mkdir inputs && #set $seen = [] #set $input_files = [] #for $i, $dataset in enumerate($input_format.input) ## mirtop names each sample after its input file, so stage files under their (unique) dataset names. ## Each file gets its own directory because mirtop writes <name>.bam and <name>_sort.bam next to it ## and reuses them if they already exist. #set $sample = re.sub(r'(?i)\.(bam|sam|mirna|txt|tsv|tabular)$', '', str($dataset.element_identifier)) #set $sample = re.sub(r'[^\w\-.]', '_', $sample).strip('.') or 'sample' #set $base = $sample #set $n = 1 #while $sample in $seen #set $n += 1 #set $sample = '%s_%d' % ($base, $n) #end while #silent $seen.append($sample) #if $input_format.format == 'BAM' #if $dataset.is_of_type('sam') #set $staged = 'inputs/%d/%s.sam' % ($i, $sample) #else #set $staged = 'inputs/%d/%s.bam' % ($i, $sample) #end if #else #set $staged = 'inputs/%d/%s.txt' % ($i, $sample) #end if #silent $input_files.append($staged) mkdir 'inputs/$i' && ln -s '$dataset' '$staged' && #end for @STAGE_ANNOTATION@ #if str($keep_name) and len($input_files) > 1 ## with read names kept, mirtop writes one line per sample for the same sequence echo 'Keeping the read name only works with a single input file.' >&2 && exit 1 && #end if mirtop gff --format '$input_format.format' --hairpin hairpin.fa --gtf annotation.gff3 --sps '$sps' #if str($database) not in ('', 'None') --database '$database' #end if $keep_name $add_extra -o output #for $staged in $input_files '$staged' #end for && mv output/mirtop.gff '$output'

param.label: Input format
param.option: BAM/SAM alignments against the hairpin sequences

param.name: input
param.label: Aligned reads
param.help: Reads aligned to the hairpin FASTA, e.g. with bowtie. Read names ending in _xN (as written by seqcluster collapse) are counted N times.

param.label: Annotation database
param.help: Which database the annotation GFF3 comes from. This picks how mirtop parses the annotation, so it must match the file. Leave empty to detect it from the GFF3 header.

param.label: Use the read name in the attribute column
param.help: By default reads are identified by their sequence-derived UID. Only possible with a single input file.

param.label: Add extra attributes
param.help: Adds the nucleotide changes behind each isomiR variant to the attributes.

has_text.text: only works with a single input file

tool.help:
## What it does
[mirtop](https://github.com/miRTop/mirtop) annotates small RNA-seq reads against miRNA precursors and writes the result in [mirGFF3](https://github.com/miRTop/mirGFF3), the community format for miRNA and isomiR quantification. Each line describes one unique read sequence: the mature miRNA it belongs to, how it differs from the reference miRNA (5' and 3' trimming, non-templated 3' additions, nucleotide substitutions) and its count in every sample.
All inputs are merged into one mirGFF3 file with one expression column per sample. Sample names come from the input dataset names, with a trailing file extension removed and characters other than letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.` replaced by `_`. Repeated names get `_2`, `_3` and so on.
## Inputs
- **Aligned reads**: BAM or SAM files of reads aligned to the hairpin FASTA (for example with bowtie, as nf-core/smrnaseq does). If read names end in `_xN`, as written by `seqcluster collapse`, each read counts N times; reads named any other way get an expression of 0. Alternatively, seqbuster/miraligner `.mirna` files or PROST! output can be converted. For seqbuster files the count is also read from `_xN` in the read name, not from the `freq` column. A PROST! file must hold a single sample; mirtop returns nothing for a multi-sample one. - **Hairpin sequences**: the precursor FASTA the reads were aligned to, e.g. miRBase `hairpin.fa`. Only entries whose header line contains the species code are used. - **Mature miRNA annotation**: the miRBase GFF3 for the species (e.g. `hsa.gff3`) giving the mature miRNA positions on each precursor. - **Species code**: the miRBase prefix such as `hsa` or `mmu`.
## Output
A mirGFF3 file. Its attribute column uses `key value;` pairs rather than GFF3's `key=value`, so it is stored with Galaxy's generic `gff` datatype instead of `gff3`. Use **mirtop counts** to turn it into a count table and **mirtop stats** for per-sample summaries.
